signature.name: Rock of Gibraltar
signature.detail: The limestone promontory dominates the town and gives the territory its identity. Its upper slopes are a nature reserve, home to the famous Barbary macaques, and it offers wide views across the Strait toward Africa. Wear sturdy shoes and bring water, as the paths are steep and exposed.

signature.name: St. Michael's Cave
signature.detail: A large natural limestone cave system in the Upper Rock, known for its dramatic chambers and lighting. It is one of the most popular stops on the Rock. Go early in the day to avoid the midday crowds, and expect some steps and uneven ground.

signature.name: Gibraltar Great Siege Tunnels
signature.detail: A network of tunnels cut into the rock during the Great Siege of the 1780s, used for guns and observation. They give a vivid picture of the territory's military history. Book a guided visit where possible and allow around an hour.

signature.name: Moorish Castle
signature.detail: A fortification whose origins go back to Moorish rule, with later additions from other periods. It sits on the western slopes near the town and is well suited to a relaxed walk with views. Visit in the morning or late afternoon, when it is cooler.

signature.name: Gibraltar Cable Car
signature.detail: The cable car carries visitors from the town up to the Upper Rock, saving a steep climb and giving sweeping views. It is the simplest way to reach the top. Buy tickets online ahead of busy periods and check the schedule for wind closures.

signature.name: Main Street & Casemates Square
signature.detail: The pedestrian Main Street is the heart of the old town, lined with shops, cafes and British-style buildings. Casemates Square is a lively gathering point with restaurants. Visit in the evening when the square is busiest.

food: Casual meal $10-18; fish and chips about $12
transport: Bus $1-2 a ride; cable car about $25-30 return; taxis short trips $5-10
